verses.sanskrit:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच।
              तस्मिन्नन्तर्हिते देवे वचनात्तस्य वै प्रभोः। चक्षुर्दिव्यं सविज्ञानं प्रादुरासीत्तदा मम॥१॥
ततोऽहं तानपश्यं वै ब्राह्मणान्कौशिकात्मजान्। आपगेय कुरुक्षेत्रे यानुवाच विभुर्मम॥२॥
verses.bhavadeepa: विंशेऽत्र वर्ण्यते ब्रह्मदत्तः उग्रायुधस्तथा। पूजनीयकथा शुक्रप्रोक्ता नीतिरनुत्तमा॥१॥ तस्मिन्निति॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मदत्तोऽभवद्राजा यस्तेषां सप्तमो द्विजः। पितृवर्तीति विख्यातो नाम्ना शीलेन कर्मणा॥३॥
verses.english: Of those seven brAhmaNA-s, the seventh one who is famous for his deeds and conduct, because he is true to his name पितृ-वर्ति, a father-devotee, later took birth as king ब्रह्मदत्त, and became a best king of काम्पिल्य city... the daughter of शुक, lady कृत्वि, aka कीर्ति-मति, begot this ब्रह्मदत्त through a king called अणुहु..." So said mArkanDeya to bhIShma.
verses.bhavadeepa: तान् पूर्वं भरद्वाजदायादान् सतः द्वितीये जन्मनि कुरुक्षेत्रे कौशिकात्मजान् अपश्यम्। आपगेय हे भीष्म विभुः सनत्कुमारः॥२॥

verses.sanskrit: शुकस्य कन्या कृत्वी तं जनयामास पार्थिवम्। अणुहात्पार्थिवश्रेष्ठात्काम्पिल्ये नगरोत्तमे॥४॥
verses.english: Thus, this is the twentieth chapter of first canto called harivamsha-parva, in harivamsha-purANa, the sequel of mahAbhArata, narrating the legends of rebellious warrior उग्र-आयुध and a lady bird called पूजनीय.
verses.bhavadeepa: तेषां कुशिकात्मजानां यः सप्तमो द्विजः पितृवर्ती नाम स एव सप्तमे जन्मनि ब्रह्मदत्तोऽभवत्॥३॥

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              यथोवाच महाभागो मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः। तस्य वंशमहं राजन्कीर्तयिष्यामि तच्छृणु॥५॥
verses.english: "Oh, dharmaja...this is what sage mArkanDeya said to me and I am now reiterating the same to you..." Thus bhIShma is reiterating to dharmaja.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              अणुहः कस्य वै पुत्रः कस्मिन्काले बभूव ह। राजा धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठो यस्य पुत्रो महायशाः॥६॥
verses.english: I for myself balefully committed an outrageous deed of blinding your son; hence my reposal of any trust in you, now onwards, is out of question

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मदत्तो नरपतिः किंवीर्यः स बभूव ह। कथं च सप्तमस्तेषां स बभूव नराधिपः॥७॥
verses.english: Highly renowned yoga-master गालव, who studiously rearranged the texts of वेद-अन्ग-s, ancillaries of veda-s, up to some extent, is the collegian - सह-पाठि - and a confidant of this brahmadatta...

verses.sanskrit: न ह्यल्पवीर्याय शुको भगवाँल्लोकपूजितः। कन्यां प्रादाद्यद्योगात्मा कृत्वीं कीर्तिमतीं प्रभुः॥८॥
verses.english: Another soul of honour, namely कण्डरीक, is his best minister... in fact, all his consociates are like that... that is to say, the king, his ministers, and friends... all are - ब्रह्म-वेत्ता-s - proficient in the quiddity of brahma... further, brahmadatta has seven such friends in all his previous seven births, of whom गालव is cited because he is a prominent one...

verses.sanskrit: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण महाद्युते। ब्रह्मदत्तस्य चरितं तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति॥९॥
verses.english: King brahmadatta is from the lineage of पुरु dynasty... hence listen about the lineage of पुरु kings as has been said by sage mArkanDeya...

verses.sanskrit: यथा च वर्तमानास्ते संसारे च द्विजातयः। मार्कण्डेयेन कथितास्तद्भवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे॥१०॥
verses.english: Vestigial debt, fire, or a foe redoubles in no time... hence, oh, king brahmadatta, their remains should not remain...

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              प्रतीपस्य तु राजर्षेस्तुल्यकालो नराधिप। पितामहस्य मे राजन्बभूवेति मया श्रुतम्॥११॥
verses.english: King हस्ति begot three sons, namely अज-मीढ, द्वि-मीढ, and पुरु-मीढ; king अज-मीढ begot a son named बृहद्-इषु through lady धूमिनि; बृहत्-धनु is the son of बृहय्-इषु...

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मदत्तो महाभागो योगी राजर्षिसत्तमः। रुतज्ञः सर्वभूतानां सर्वभूतहिते रतः॥१२॥
verses.english: Though हरि, epithetically इन्द्र here, outwardly made an accord with sages to not to do any duplicity, furtively eliminated demon नमुचि, that too just with the spume of ocean water in which his weapon thunderbolt is camouflaged...

verses.sanskrit: सखाऽऽस गालवो यस्य योगाचार्यो महायशाः। शिक्षामुत्पाद्य तपसा क्रमो येन प्रवर्तितः। कण्डरीकश्च योगात्मा तस्यैव सचिवो महान्॥१३॥
verses.english: And this नीप begot hundred sons, who are highly resplendent, valiant, mighty of mightiest, and who are the top speeded men-at-chariots... and they are collectively called 'नीपा-s' after their father...

verses.sanskrit: जात्यन्तरेषु सर्वेषु सखायः सर्व एव ते। सप्तजातिषु सप्तैव बभूवुरमितौजसः। यथोवाच महाभागो मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः॥१४॥
verses.english: Another soul of honour, namely कण्डरीक, is his best minister... in fact, all his consociates are like that... that is to say, the king, his ministers, and friends... all are - ब्रह्म-वेत्ता-s - proficient in the quiddity of brahma... further, brahmadatta has seven such friends in all his previous seven births, of whom गालव is cited because he is a prominent one...
verses.bhavadeepa: सखा आसेति पदच्छेदः। आसीदित्यर्थः। शिक्षां वेदाङ्गं क्रमः संहितायाः पदानां सहपाठः। अन्नाद्यकामो निर्भुजं ब्रूयात्स्वर्गकामः प्रतृण्णमुभयकाम उभयमन्तरेणेति श्रुतिप्रसिद्ध एव पूर्वैरज्ञानादप्रवर्तितः सन् गालवेन प्रवर्तित इत्यर्थः। तस्य ब्रह्मदत्तस्य॥१३॥

verses.sanskrit: तस्य वंशमहं राजन्कीर्तयिष्यामि तच्छृणु। ब्रह्मदत्तस्य पौराणां पौरवस्य महात्मनः॥१५॥
verses.english: Taking heed of the following maixim, people strive to eradicate any trace of enmity for fear of its recurrence...
verses.bhavadeepa: सप्तजातिषु सप्तसु जन्मसु ते सप्त परस्परं सहाया बभूवुरिति सम्बन्धः॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: बृहत्क्षत्रस्य दायादः सुहोत्रो नाम धार्मिकः। सुहोत्रस्यापि दायादो हस्ती नाम बभूव ह॥१६॥
verses.english: King समर has three highly righteous sons, namely पर, पार, सदश्व; पार begot a son called पृथु, who is highly proficient in dharma; then पृथु by virtue of his good deeds begot a prince called सुकृत - behovely; then that सुकृत begot a prince called विभ्राज; later विभ्राज begot अणुहु, who is the husband of lady कृत्वि, thus the son-in-law of highly renowned शुक॥। This अणुहु is the coeval of my grandfather प्रतीप...." Thus bhIShma is continuing his narration to dharmaja.

verses.sanskrit: तेनेदं निर्मितं पूर्वं हस्तिनापुरमुत्तमम्। हस्तिनश्चापि दायादास्त्रयः परमधार्मिकाः॥१७॥
verses.english: Then ब्रह्मदत्त, the sagely king and the honourable soul of yoga is the son of king अणुहु; then ब्रह्मदत्त'स् son is विष्वक्सेन॥। they say, विभ्राज, the deceased father of अणुहु, reacquiring mortal life owing to his past deeds took rebirth as this विष्वक्सेन॥।

verses.sanskrit: अजमीढो द्विमीढश्च पुरुमीढस्तथैव च। अजमीढस्य धूमिन्यां जज्ञे बृहदिषुर्नृप। बृहद्धनुर्बृहदिषोः पुत्रस्तस्य महायशाः॥१८॥
verses.english: Unbelievable is an enmy even if he conducts himself smilingly, facetiously, or shares a meal in a single plate, or takes a single seat... hence there should be no interconnection or interdependence with him...

verses.sanskrit: बृहद्धर्मेति विख्यातो राजा परमधार्मिकः। सत्यजित्तनयस्तस्य विश्वजित्तस्य चात्मजः॥१९॥
verses.english: People will strive to eliminate their enemies when in slumber, drunk or unwary... especially by poison, arson, or dissimulations...

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रो विश्वजितश्चापि सेनजित्पृथिवीपतिः। पुत्राः सेनजितश्चासंश्चत्वारो लोकविश्रुताः॥२०॥
verses.english: विष्वक्सेन'स् son is दण्डसेन whose son is भल्लाट whom one called राधेय has slain... this भल्लाट, the son of दण्डसेन is a true valiant, highsouled person and conserved his family prestige...

verses.sanskrit: रुचिरः श्वेतकेतुश्च महिम्नारस्तथैव च। वत्सश्चावन्तको राजा यस्यैते परिवत्सकाः॥२१॥
verses.english: Thus these are the aphoristic teachings contained in उश्नो-गीत rendered by श्रुक्राचार्य, and he who assimilates them and put to use for his self-defence is a wise man

verses.sanskrit: रुचिरस्य तु दायादः पृथुसेनो महायशाः। पृथुसेनस्य पारस्तु पारान्नीपस्तु जज्ञिवान्॥२२॥
verses.english: "Whose son is this उग्र-आयुध... to which family he belongs... what for he had to be eliminated by you... please tell me something about it..." thus yudhiShThira cross-queried bhIShma...
verses.bhavadeepa: आवन्तको अवन्त्यां भवो राजा सेनजित्। यस्य एते रुचिरादयः परिवत्सकाः पुत्राः॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: नीपस्यैकशतं तात पुत्राणाममितौजसाम्। महारथानां राजेन्द्र शूराणां बाहुशालिनाम्। नीपा इति समाख्याता राजानः सर्व एव ते॥२३॥
verses.english: The prince सर्व-सेन daily used to bring the baby bird from the nest to ground and started to play with it, as and when the mother bird pUjanIya went out of the palace in the morning on her daily rounds...

verses.sanskrit: तेषां वंशकरो राजा नीपानां किर्तिवर्धनः। काम्पिल्ये समरो नाम सचेष्टसमरोऽभवत्॥२४॥
समरस्य परः पारः सदश्व इति ते त्रयः। पुत्राः परमधर्मज्ञाः परपुत्रः पृथुर्बभौ॥२५॥
verses.english: Unlivable in the proximity of enemy while animosity is escalating for it leads to one's own fall as the rush of river's current undercuts trees living on riverbanks...

verses.sanskrit: पृथोस्तु सुकृतो नाम सुकृतेनेह कर्मणा। जज्ञे सर्वगुणोपेतो विभ्राजस्तस्य चात्मजः॥२६॥
verses.english: Highly renowned yoga-master गालव, who studiously rearranged the texts of वेद-अन्ग-s, ancillaries of veda-s, up to some extent, is the collegian - सह-पाठि - and a confidant of this brahmadatta...

verses.sanskrit: विभ्राजस्य तु पुत्रोऽभूदणुहो नाम पार्थिवः। बभौ शुकस्य जामाता कृत्वीभर्ता महायशाः॥२७॥
verses.english: This कार्ति or कीर्ति is the father of the valiant legatee of पौरव-s, namely उग्र-आयुध, who attacked and slain the then king of पान्चाल, a legatee of नीप and the grandsire of पृषत॥।

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रोऽणुहस्य राजर्षिर्ब्रह्मदत्तोऽभवत्प्रभुः। योगात्मा तस्य तनयो विष्वक्सेनः परन्तपः॥२८॥
verses.english: The progeny of ugra-Ayudha is like this: उग्र-आयुध क्षेम्य सु-वीर नृपञ्जय, or सृञ्जय बहु-रथ... these will be called the legatees of पौरव-s...

verses.sanskrit: विभ्राजः पुनरायातः स्वकृतेनेह कर्मणा। ब्रह्मदत्तस्य पुत्रोऽन्यः सर्वसेन इति श्रुतः॥२९॥
verses.english: That mighty king उग्र-आयुध acquired a fierce weapon, namely a disc, purportedly per kindness of shrI hari, so they say... and then he started to wipe out नीप dynasty... having annihilated the kings of नीप and other kings incidentally, his audacity multiplied making him a pervert...
verses.bhavadeepa: पुत्र इति। तस्य ब्रह्मदत्तस्य तनयो विष्वक्सेनो नाम स च योगात्मा योगेन धृतशरीरः॥२८॥

verses.sanskrit: चक्षुषी तस्य निर्भिन्ने पक्षिण्या पूजनीयया। सुचिरोषितया राजन्ब्रह्मदत्तस्य वेश्मनि॥३०॥
verses.english: At that time my father king शन्तनु breathed his last, and I was undertaking पितृ-मेध, postfunerary rites, with utmost sincerity like dietaries and getting forty winks on bare ground etc... at such a time this ugra-Ayudha sent a messenger to me when I am surrounded by my ministers, who conveyed a worst message to me...
verses.bhavadeepa: एतदेव व्याचष्टे- विभ्राज इति। विभ्राजो ब्रह्मदत्तस्य पितामहः। स्वकृतेन वक्ष्यमाणेन कर्मणा विष्वक्सेनरूपेण पुनरिमं लोकं ब्रह्मदतः पुत्रो भूत्वा आयात इत्यर्थः॥२९॥

verses.sanskrit: अथास्य पुत्रस्त्वपरो ब्रह्मदत्तस्य जज्ञिवान्। विष्वक्सेन इति ख्यातो महाबलपराक्रमः॥३१॥
verses.english: Coming into my audience, oh, king dharmaja, that messenger of ugra-Ayudha parroted these words of his sender: "oh, bhIShma, yield your glorious stepmother, a jewel among women, as my makeshift-wife...

verses.sanskrit: विष्वक्सेनस्य पुत्रोऽभूद्दण्डसेनो महीपतिः। भल्लाटोऽस्य कुमारोऽभूद्राधेयेन हतः पुरा॥३२॥
verses.english: Whereby oh, कुरु, the great... you can snowball your kingdom and riches... no doubt about it... or, I will present whatever gems and jewels available on earth if you so wish... or else, see the indomitable discus of mine that is ablaze, just by the sight of which my enemies fleeth the battlefield... if you cherish well-being of your province, or of your life, or of your dynasty, simply remain in my command... otherwise, you have no peace...

verses.sanskrit: दण्डसेनात्मजः शूरो महात्मा कुलवर्धनः। भल्लाटपुत्रो दुर्बुद्धिरभवच्च युधिष्ठिर॥३३॥
verses.english: This is the message sent to someone who is observing ritual formalities like reposing on mats on ground etc... actually, I too was reposing on a mat then... but perceiving the malice of उग्र-आयुध through such a message that is twingeing like the tongue of an inferno, I then got up, dismissed the messenger, ordered all of my army commanders to be at the ready...

verses.sanskrit: स तेषामभवद्राजा नीपानामन्तकृन्नृप। उग्रायुधेन यस्यार्थे सर्वे नीपा विनाशिताः॥३४॥
verses.english: At that time, विcइत्रवीर्य was just a boy and wholly dependant on me... perceiving उग्र-आयुध, is hell-bent on warring with me as he is maddened with fury, I too wanted to retaliate... but, my ministers who are experts in political thinking, my priests who are high scholars of vedic injunctions, my friends who are well aware of the expedient, and the other near and dear who all base their thinking in scriptural imperatives have deterred me from a direct confrontation at that particular moment... they have advised me about some workable methods that can be undertaken at that time, i.e., when I am in postfunerary vow aimed at my deceased father...

verses.sanskrit: उग्रायुधो मदोत्सिक्तो मया विनिहतो युधि। दर्पान्वितो दर्परुचिः सततं चानये रतः॥३५॥
verses.english: That sinister उग्र-आयुध'स् discus is still spinning, my lord, for it is godsend to him..., and when you are in an unclean state - अशौचम् - ceremonially impure condition, it is not advisable to confront a weapon of divine origin... so, a direct war is not the immediate solution, anywise... hence, we the ministers will approach the intruder using political traits of साम, दान, भेद उपाया-s, tactics of amity, integrity, and dis-integrity, to alleviate a confrontation... should this fail, you may wage a war after cleansing yourself at the end of postfunerary vow towards your deceased father... after completion of this vow of yours, you have to take the cleansing ceremonial bath; then firstly worship gods; obtain sacred blessings of priests - स्वस्ति-अयन-वाक्या-s; enkindle sacred ritual fires; venerate scholarly brAhmaNA-s; then, having received the consent of scholars, you can embark on a battle, if you cherish a righteous victory...

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              उग्रायुधः कस्य सुतः कस्मिन्वंशेऽथ जज्ञिवान्। किमर्थं चैव भवता निहतस्तद्ब्रवीहि मे॥३६॥

भीष्म उवाच।
              अजमीढस्य दायादो विद्वान्राजा यवीनरः। धृतिमांस्तस्य पुत्रस्तु तस्य सत्यधृतिः सुतः॥३७॥
verses.english: If the enemy is unyielding to us even after our using political tactics of amity, charity, and disintegrity, then you can launch a full-scale war to eliminate him, as indra once eliminated शम्बर-असुर, the demon, in war..." So said the ministers to me...

verses.sanskrit: जज्ञे सत्यधृतेः पुत्रो दृढनेमिः प्रतापवान्। दृढनेमिसुतश्चापि सुधर्मा नाम पार्थिवः॥३८॥
verses.english: And I, thinking that we should be heedful of the timely advice of knowledgeable people that too of elders, refrained myself from waging an immediate war... then those scholarly ministers and priests have gone to उग्र-आयुध to draw truce and I have completed the ritual vow in the meantime...

verses.sanskrit: आसीत्सुधर्मणः पुत्रः सार्वभौमः प्रजेश्वरः। सार्वभौम इति ख्यातः पृथिव्यामेकराड्विभुः॥३९॥
verses.english: But, I have been thinking all the while that 'this evil-minded उग्र-आयुध will not yield to any of the political manoeuvres preplanned by my ministers...' 'his discus will be effective if he uses it properly... how can that so-called divine discus will work for his gains when he himself became a wife-snatcher...' 'I have no knowledge of the capability of that discus... how to backfire it, if at all it is launched on us...' these being my thoughts, good samaritans have also inveighed him saying, 'this उग्र-आयुध is digging his own grave by this provocative action...'

verses.sanskrit: तस्यान्ववाये महति महान्पौरवनन्दन। महतश्चापि पुत्रस्तु राजा रुक्मरथः स्मृतः॥४०॥
verses.english: When the delegation of my ministers failed, as expected, I set out to encounter the enemy myself, because my ritual vow is completed by then... when I just came out of our city, taking my arms, riding on my chariot, while priests chanting hymns for bon voyage, I am suddenly beset by enemy's army... then coming into direct confrontation, a mad war of three days is waged with the personal as well as the might of our armies, as if it is a war between gods and demons... "And oh, enemy-eliminator dharmaja, that उग्र-आयुध, burnt by the efficacy of my missile fell down in the van of battle, and breathed his last...

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रो रुक्मरथस्यापि सुपार्श्वो नाम पार्थिवः। सुपार्श्वतनयश्चापि सुमतिर्नाम धार्मिकः॥४१॥
verses.english: A while later king पृषत came back to throne of काम्पिल्य, viz. south पान्चाल, as he had to back away from his kingdom when his grandfather and the lord of नीप-s is dead at the hand of उग्र-आयुध, while that उग्र-आयुध, the then ruling king of पान्चाल, is dead at my hand...

verses.sanskrit: सुमतेरपि धर्मात्मा सन्नतिर्नाम वीर्यवान्। तस्य वै सन्नतेः पुत्रः कृतो नाम महाबलः॥४२॥
verses.english: This king पृषत, the father of king द्रुपद, ruled both south पान्चाल with capital काम्पिल्य, as well as the north pAnchAla with capital आहि-च्छत्रं, of course, with the carte blanche given by me...

verses.sanskrit: शिष्यो हिरण्यनाभस्य कौशलस्य महात्मनः। चतुर्विंशतिधा तेन सप्राच्याः सामसंहिताः॥४३॥
verses.english: This prince कृत is the disciple of a vedic-teacher from कोसल province called हिरण्य-नाभ... this teacher has bifurcated old treatises of साम-वेद into twenty-four divisions that are later renowned as प्राच्य-सामा-स्, ancient sAma-veda-hymns; कार्ति, the son of कृत has practised the singing of these sAma-veda-hymns in the rearranged method, hence those who sing sAma-hymns in that way are called as कीर्ति-साम-गा - कीर्ति-साम-singers - prefixing the name of original singer to the method of singing, with a little variation in words कार्ति and कीर्ति...

verses.sanskrit: स्मृतास्ते प्राच्यसामानः कार्तयो नाम सामगाः। कार्तिरुग्रायुधः सोऽथ वीरः पौरवनन्दनः॥४४॥
verses.english: Thus this is the dynastic legend of drupada and others, brahmadatta, nIpa kings and that of ugra-Ayudha, narrated in its entirety...

verses.sanskrit: बभूव येन विक्रम्य पृषतस्य पितामहः। नीपो नाम महतेजाः पाञ्चालाधिपतिर्हतः॥४५॥
verses.english: "h गाङ्गेय, what for the bird पूजनीय pecked off the eyes of brahmadatta's son? Though that bird is house-trained, though it has stay put in the palace for a long time, how come that bird harmed the inmates... basically, what for that bird remained in the palace of brahmadatta for a long time... what is the attachment between that king and this bird.... please clarify these doubts of mine...
verses.bhavadeepa: कार्तिः कृतस्य पुत्रः येन पञ्चालाधिपतिर्हत इति सम्बन्धः॥४४॥

verses.sanskrit: उग्रायुधस्य दायादः क्षेम्यो नाम महायशाः। क्षेम्यात्सुवीरो नृपतिः सुवीरात्तु नृपञ्जयः॥४६॥
नृपञ्जयाद्बहुरथ इत्येते पौरवाः स्मृताः। स चाप्युग्रायुधस्तात दुर्बुद्धिरभवत्तदा॥४७॥
verses.english: There used to be a preen bird named पूजनीय, a dear friend of brahmadatta, which is beauteous with coppery plume, white wings, and whitely white dorsally and ventrally... the brahmadatta's palace has become that bird's accustomed snuggery whereby that king is emotionally attached to this bird...

verses.sanskrit: प्रवृद्धचक्रो बलवान्नीपान्तकरणो महान्। स दर्पपूर्णो हत्वाऽऽजौ नीपानन्यांश्च पार्थिवान्॥४८॥
verses.english: Everyday that bird, exiting the royal palace, used to flutter over seashores, rivers, and lakes; it used to roam in the forests and gardens on the mountain terraces where just grown leaflets are there; on the lakes filled with plenitude of blossomy flowers; where the breeze is loaded with the fragrances of the pollen of lotuses, कुमुद and उत्पल etc flowers; and where the ambience is reverberating with the coos of hosts of swans, सारस, कारण्डव etc waterfowls...

verses.sanskrit: पितर्युपरते मह्यं श्रावयामास किल्बिषम्। माममात्यैः परिवृतं शयानं धरणीतले॥४९॥
verses.english: That bird used to return to kAmpilya city by the evening after moving like that through out the day... then, on coming back to the palace of king brahmadatta that bird used to narrate if any amazing things or happenings she has seen on that day, like a daily newscaster...

verses.sanskrit: उग्रायुधस्य राजेन्द्र दूतोऽभ्येत्य वचोऽब्रवीत्। अद्य त्वं जननीं भीष्म गन्धकालीं यशस्विनीम्। स्त्रीरत्नं मम भार्यार्थे प्रयच्छ कुरुपुङ्गव॥५०॥
verses.english: Coming into my audience, oh, king dharmaja, that messenger of ugra-Ayudha parroted these words of his sender: "oh, bhIShma, yield your glorious stepmother, a jewel among women, as my makeshift-wife...

verses.sanskrit: एवं राज्यं च ते स्फीतं धनानि च न संशयः। प्रदास्यामि यथाकाममहं वै रत्नभाग्भुवि॥५१॥
verses.english: However, the mother bird pUjanIya had shown equal tenderness towards the two newborns, her son, and the prince सर्व-सेन, day in and day out... she used to bring two nectarine fruits daily by evening for these two infants, because eating them is synonymous with consuming nectar itself for those two... mother bird's bringing two fruits and the infants eating them has become a daily routine...

verses.sanskrit: मम प्रज्वलितं चक्रं निशम्येदं सुदुर्जयम्। शत्रवो विद्रवन्त्याजौ दर्शनादेव भारत॥५२॥
verses.english: The prince सर्व-सेन daily used to bring the baby bird from the nest to ground and started to play with it, as and when the mother bird pUjanIya went out of the palace in the morning on her daily rounds...

verses.sanskrit: राष्ट्रस्येच्छसि चेत्स्वस्ति प्राणानां वा कुलस्य वा। शासने मम तिष्ठस्व न हि ते शान्तिरन्यथा॥५३॥
verses.english: On certain day when the prince wanted to play with young bird, he dragged it from the nest, but it resisted... he again pulled it catching by its neck... being a frail bird it could not free itself from the tight grip of the prince, and breathed its last instantaneously...

verses.sanskrit: अधः प्रस्तारशयने शयानस्तेन चोदितः। दूतान्तर्हितमेतद्वै वाक्यमग्निशिखोपमम्॥५४॥
verses.english: Arriving from somewhere, king brahmadatta saw that dead baby bird in the hands of prince, and understood that the prince alone has strangulated the bird to death, and somehow released the dead bird from the grip of the prince, making it fall to ground... then, clutching the ground where the dead bird has fallen, the king wailed tearfully... he remained squatted on ground lamenting for the bird...

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहं तस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्विज्ञाय मतमच्युत। आज्ञापयं वै सङ्ग्रामे सेनाध्यक्षांश्च सर्वशः॥५५॥
verses.english: At the same time the mother bird pUjanIya also returned to the palace of brahmadatta taking two nectarine fruits. ब्रह्मदत्त who is lamenting for the departed baby bird also noticed the arrival of mother bird... but became speechless in his mourning. On seeing her baby bird, from which the five vital elements have departed, and lay dead, that mother bird fainted instantaneously... recovering her senses later she wailed a lot...

verses.sanskrit: विचित्रवीर्यं बालं च मदुपाश्रयमेव च। दृष्ट्वा क्रोधपरीतात्मा युद्धायैव मनो दधे॥५६॥
verses.english: "O, son why you are not nearing me today... why don't you make sweet sounds with your sweet voice... why you don't bite this fruit today with your yellow beak... why don't you eat this fruit with your reddish mouth... why not wiggle your wings to my delight... why I am not listening your pleasant chirping saying चि-ची-कू-ची... if not now, when can my motherly affection be fulfilled with a son like you... opening your mouth and wiggling your wings you used to ask for water... where is it now... all my motherly hopes are shattered with your passing..." thus that mother bird wailed a lot and then started questioning the king...

verses.sanskrit: निगृहीतस्तदाहं तैः सचिवैर्मन्त्रकोविदैः। ऋत्विग्भिर्वेदकल्पैश्च सुहृद्भिश्चार्थदर्शिभिः॥५७॥
verses.english: "O, king you are a king anointed scripturally and you are well aware of age-old tradition... tell me you lowly kshatriya... what for you made my son fall dead at the hand your son who strangled him... are you heedless of the canons of अङ्गीरस-स्...
verses.bhavadeepa: बालं दृष्ट्वा बालोऽयं युद्धायोग्य इति ज्ञात्वाऽहमेव युद्धाय मनो दधे धृतवान्॥५६॥

verses.sanskrit: स्निग्धैश्च शास्त्रविद्भिश्च संयुगस्य निवर्तने। कारणं श्रावितश्चास्मि युक्तरूपं तदानघ॥५८॥
verses.english: "One who does not protect him, who is in need of shelter, thirsty, hungry; or one who is fleeing for fear of foes; or one who is long-time resident in his own house, will undoubtedly fall in a hell called कुंभी-पाक-नरकम्..." so say the canons of अङ्गीरस-s... then, where is the question of gods or fatherly-gods taking the holy-oblations offered by such a hell-bound person..

verses.sanskrit:
मन्त्रिण ऊचुः।
              प्रवृत्तचक्रः पापोऽसौ त्वं चाशौचगतः प्रभो। न चैष प्रथमः कल्पो युद्धं नाम कदाचन॥५९॥
verses.english: Saying so she that mother bird went into a state called tenfold-frenzy induced by her ecstatic wailing, Then, on puncturing the eyes of the son of brahmadatta with her talons and rendering him blind she dashed to sky...

verses.sanskrit: ते वयं सामपूर्वं वै दानं भेदं तथैव च। प्रयोक्ष्यामस्ततः शुद्धो दैवतान्यभिवाद्य च॥६०॥
verses.english: Even on seeing his son blinded that way, king brahmadatta spoke to the mother bird in this way, "you have justly requited like for like with my son... oh, lady-bird, be fearless and leave off your agony... you have done whatever you ought to... even though I am heartbroken for my son, I don't bear a grudge against you for whatever you have done to him... come back and stay with me as before...
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रवृत्तेति। उच्छृङ्खलप्रवृत्तेः शास्त्रनियन्त्रितस्य च युद्धं प्रथमो मुख्यः कल्पो न भवतीत्यर्थः॥५९॥

verses.sanskrit: कृतस्वस्त्ययनो विप्रैर्हुत्वाग्नीनर्च्य च द्विजान्। ब्राह्मणैरभ्यनुज्ञातः प्रयास्यसि जयाय वै॥६१॥
verses.english: "Committing the blunder of blinding your son, oh, kingly tiger, it will be unbefitting for me to stay further in your house... I am aware of your love for your soul-like son...

verses.sanskrit: अस्त्राणि च प्रयोज्यानि न प्रवेश्यश्च सङ्गरः। आशौचे वर्तमाने तु वृद्धानामिति शासनम्॥६२॥
verses.english: You may list4en to शुक्र-नीति as I tell... a vile-friend, vile-country, vile-king, vile-friend, vile-son, vile-wife are discardable distantly...

verses.sanskrit: सामदानादिभिः पूर्णमपि भेदेन वा ततः। तां हनिष्यसि विक्रम्य शम्बरं मघवानिव॥६३॥
verses.english: Where is amity with a vile-friend, where is the pleasure with a vile-wife, where is beatification with a vilely son, where is candour with a vile-king, where is trustfulness with a vilely person, where is livelihood in a vilest country! Threat haunts everywhere from a vile-king, while fret hangs around everything from a vile-son...

verses.sanskrit: प्राज्ञानां वचनं काले वृद्धानां च विशेषतः। श्रोतव्यमिति तच्छ्रुत्वा निवृत्तोऽस्मि नराधिप॥६४॥
verses.english: A basely fellow becomes debilitated, deprived, or even short-lived, if he reposes confidence in deleterious people... reposing confidence in untrustworthy is bad; reposing overconfidence in trustworthy is equally bad, because confidence breeds compunction, which uproots root and branch of the truster...

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तैः सङ्क्रमः सर्वः प्रयुक्तः शास्त्रकोविदैः। तस्मिन्काले कुरुश्रेष्ठ कर्म चारब्धमुत्तमम्॥६५॥
verses.english: A fool reposing confidence in the officials of the king, or in the misbegotten nitwits, will not have a long-lived life...

verses.sanskrit: स सामादिभिरेवादावुपायैः प्राज्ञचिन्तितैः। अनुनीयमानो दुर्बुद्धिरनुनेतुं न शक्यते॥६६॥
verses.english: Presumptuous self-styled elevation of oneself higher than a king ruins him instantaneously as with an ant falling to death when it soars to heights just when its wings started to emerge...

verses.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तं तस्य तच्चक्रमधर्मनिरतस्य वै। परदाराभिलाषेण सद्यस्तात निवर्तितम्॥६७॥
verses.english: If one is succumbed to the cajolery of his enemy it is his self-ruin as with a great tree succumbing to the entanglement of a creeper around it...

verses.sanskrit: न त्वहं तस्य जाने तन्निवृत्तं चक्रमुत्तमम्। हतं स्वकर्मणा तं तु पूर्वं सद्भिश्च निन्दितम्॥६८॥
verses.english: If one believes an enemy beguiled by his sweet and juicy talk his fate is doomed as with a tree slowly gouged out by a snake pit...

verses.sanskrit: कृतशौचः शरी चापी रथी निष्क्रम्य वै पुरात्। कृतस्वस्त्ययनो विप्रैः प्रायोधयमहं रिपुम्॥६९॥
verses.english: Though हरि, epithetically इन्द्र here, outwardly made an accord with sages to not to do any duplicity, furtively eliminated demon नमुचि, that too just with the spume of ocean water in which his weapon thunderbolt is camouflaged...
verses.bhavadeepa: अहं तस्य चक्रम् आज्ञानिवृत्तं भग्नमिति जाने। तं स्वकर्मणा हतं जाने॥६८॥

verses.sanskrit: ततः संसर्गमागम्य बलेनास्त्रबलेन च। त्र्यहमुन्मत्तवद्युद्धं देवासुरमिवाभवत्॥७०॥
verses.english: People will strive to eliminate their enemies when in slumber, drunk or unwary... especially by poison, arson, or dissimulations...

verses.sanskrit: स मयास्त्रप्रतापेन निर्दग्धो रणमूर्धनि। पपाताभिमुखः शूरस्त्यक्त्वा प्राणानरिन्दम॥७१॥
verses.english: Taking heed of the following maixim, people strive to eradicate any trace of enmity for fear of its recurrence...

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तात काम्पिल्ये पृषतोऽभ्ययात्। हते नीपेश्वरे चैव हते चोग्रायुधे नृपे॥७२॥
verses.english: Vestigial debt, fire, or a foe redoubles in no time... hence, oh, king brahmadatta, their remains should not remain...

verses.sanskrit: आहिच्छत्रं स्वकं राज्यं पित्र्यं प्राप महाद्युतिः। द्रुपदस्य पिता राजन्ममैवानुमते तदा॥७३॥
verses.english: If one believes an enemy beguiled by his sweet and juicy talk his fate is doomed as with a tree slowly gouged out by a snake pit...
verses.bhavadeepa: काम्पिल्ये दक्षिणपाञ्चाले नीपेश्वरे पृषतस्य पितामहे उग्रायुधेन हते उग्रायुधे च भीष्मेण हते सतीति विवेकः॥७२॥

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽर्जुनेन तरसा निर्जित्य द्रुपदं रणे। आहिच्छत्रं सकाम्पिल्यं द्रोणायाथापवर्जितम्॥७४॥
verses.english: indra is the son-in-law of पुलोम... be that as it may... the same indra eliminated पुलोम in a given war... enmity is intransigent... believing someone who comes nigh exchanging pleasantries by hiding hatred in heart is as good as adopting the syndrome 'hart-finding-a-credible-hunter...'

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य ततो द्रोण उभयं जयतां वरः। काम्पिल्यं द्रुपदायैव प्रायच्छद्विदितं तव॥७५॥
verses.english: Unlivable in the proximity of enemy while animosity is escalating for it leads to one's own fall as the rush of river's current undercuts trees living on riverbanks...

verses.sanskrit: एष ते द्रुपदस्यादौ ब्रह्मदत्तस्य चैव ह। वंशः कार्त्स्येन वै प्रोक्तो नीपस्योग्रायुधस्य च॥७६॥
verses.english: One cannot remain in self-approbation with a monologic saying 'I am at the zenith...' that too, when that stature is fed upon the interests of his enemy... he and his stature are likely to fall like a winged ant who takes flight overconfident of its trifling wings

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              किमर्थं ब्रह्मदत्तस्य पूजनीया शकुन्तिका। अन्धं चकार गाङ्गेय ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं पुरा विभो॥७७॥
verses.english: Thus these are the aphoristic teachings contained in उश्नो-गीत rendered by श्रुक्राचार्य, and he who assimilates them and put to use for his self-defence is a wise man

verses.sanskrit: चिरोषिता गृहे चापि किमर्थं चैव यस्य सा। चकार विप्रियमिदं तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः॥७८॥
verses.english: I for myself balefully committed an outrageous deed of blinding your son; hence my reposal of any trust in you, now onwards, is out of question

verses.sanskrit: पूजनीया चकारासौ किं सख्यं तेन चैव ह। एतन्मे संशयं छिन्धि सर्वमुक्त्वा यथातथम्॥७९॥
verses.english: Saying so, that lady bird पूजनीय instantaneously took wings skyward and went away... this is the episode of ब्रह्मदत्त and पूजनीय that has happened once॥। भीष्म is thus continuing narration to dharmaja.
verses.bhavadeepa: सा यस्य राज्ञो गृहे चिरोषिता तस्य विप्रियं किमर्थं चकारेत्यन्वयः॥७८॥

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              शृणु सर्वं महाराज यथावृत्तमभूत्पुरा। ब्रह्मदत्तस्य भवने तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर॥८०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: असौ पूजनीया किमर्थं तेन सख्यं चकार॥७९॥

verses.sanskrit: काचिच्छकुन्तिका राजन्ब्रह्मदत्तस्य वै सखी। शितिपक्षा शोणशिराः शितिपृष्ठा शितोदरी॥८१॥
सखी सा ब्रह्मदत्तस्य सुदृढं बद्धसौहृदा। तस्याः कुलायमभवद्गेहे तस्य नरोत्तम॥८२॥
verses.english: Oh, king धर्मज, now I will narrate further about the results occurring from the beatification of fatherly-gods, as has been said in the legends of seven-births of the sons of sage कौशिक॥ along with legends of yogi-s and ascetics like गालव, कण्डरीक and the थिर्द् ब्रह्मदत्त॥।
verses.bhavadeepa: शितिपक्षा शुक्लपक्षा शोणशिराः लोहितमस्तका शितिपृष्ठा कृष्णोपरिभागा। “शिती धवलमेचके” इति कोशकाराः॥८१॥

verses.sanskrit: सा सदाहनि निर्गत्य तस्य राज्ञो गृहोत्तमात्। चचाराम्भोधितीरेषु पल्वलेषु सरस्सु च॥८३॥
नदीपर्वतकुञ्जेषु वनेषूपवनेषु च। प्रफुल्लेषु तडागेषु कल्हारेषु सुगन्धिषु॥८४॥
कुमुदोत्पलकिञ्जल्कसुरभीकृतवायुषु। हंससारसघुष्टेषु कारण्डवरुतेषु च॥८५॥
चरित्वा तेषु सा राजन्निशि काम्पिल्यमागमत्। नृपतेर्भवनं प्राप्य ब्रह्मदत्तस्य धीमतः॥८६॥
राज्ञा तेन सदा राजन् कथायोगं चकार सा। आश्चर्याणि च दृष्टानि यानि वृत्तानि कानिचित्॥८७॥
verses.english: That bird used to return to kAmpilya city by the evening after moving like that through out the day... then, on coming back to the palace of king brahmadatta that bird used to narrate if any amazing things or happenings she has seen on that day, like a daily newscaster...

verses.sanskrit: चरित्वा विविधान्देशान्कथयामास सा निशि। कदाचित्तस्य नृपतेर्ब्रह्मदत्तस्य कौरव॥८८॥
पुत्रोऽभूद्राजशार्दूल सर्वसेनेति विश्रुतः। पूजनीयाऽथ सा तस्मिन्प्रासूताण्डमथापि च॥८९॥
तस्मिन्नीडे पुरा ह्येकं तत्किल प्रास्फुटत्तदा। स्फुटितो मांसपिण्डस्तु बाहुपादास्यसंयुतः॥९०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: सर्वसेनः इति छेदः। तस्मिन् काले गृहे च॥८९॥

verses.sanskrit: बभ्रुवक्त्रश्चक्षुर्हीनो बभूव पृथिवीपते। चक्षुष्मानप्यभूत्पश्चादीषत्पक्षोत्थितश्च ह॥९१॥
अथ सा पूजनीया वै राजपुत्रस्वपुत्रयोः। तुल्यस्नेहात्प्रीतिमती दिवसे दिवसेऽभवत्॥९२॥
verses.english: However, the mother bird pUjanIya had shown equal tenderness towards the two newborns, her son, and the prince सर्व-सेन, day in and day out... she used to bring two nectarine fruits daily by evening for these two infants, because eating them is synonymous with consuming nectar itself for those two... mother bird's bringing two fruits and the infants eating them has become a daily routine...

verses.sanskrit: आजहार सदा सायं चञ्च्वामृतफलद्वयम्। अमृतास्वादसदृशं सर्वसेनतनूजयोः॥९३॥
स बालो ब्रह्मदत्तस्य पूजनीयासुतश्च ह। ते फले भक्षयित्वा च पृथुकौ प्रीतमानसौ॥९४॥
अभूतां नित्यमेवेह खादेतां तौ च ते फले। तस्यां गतायामथ च पूजन्यां वै सदाहनि॥९५॥
शिशुना चटकेनाथ धात्री तं तु शिशुं नृप। तेन प्रक्रीडयामास ब्रह्मदत्तात्मजं सदा॥९६॥
नीडात्तमाकृष्य तदा पूजनीया कृता ततः। क्रीडता राजपुत्रेण कदाचिच्चटकः स तु॥९७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: तेन शिशुना नीडादाकृष्य धात्री तं प्रक्रीडयामास॥९६॥

verses.sanskrit: निगृहीतः कन्धरायां शिशुना दृढमुष्टिना। दुर्भङ्गमुष्टिना राजन्नसून्सद्यस्त्वजीजहत्॥९८॥
तं तु पञ्चत्वमापन्नं व्यात्तास्यं बालघातितम्। कथञ्चिन्मोचितं दृष्ट्वा नृपतिर्दुःखितोऽभवत्॥९९॥
धात्रीं तस्य जगर्हे तां तदाऽश्रुपरमो नृपः। तस्थौ शोकान्वितो राजञ्छोचंस्तं चटकं तदा॥१००॥
पूजनीयापि तत्काले गृहीत्वा तु फलद्वयम्। ब्रह्मदत्तस्य भवनमाजगाम वनेचरी॥१०१॥
अथापश्यत्तमागम्य गृहे तस्मिन्नराधिप। पञ्चभूतपरित्यक्तं शोच्यं तं स्वतनूद्भवम्॥१०२॥
मुमोह दृष्ट्वा तं पुत्रं पुन्ः संज्ञामथालभत्। लब्धसंज्ञा च सा राजन्विललाप तपस्विनी॥१०३॥

पूजनीयोवाच।
              न तु त्वमागतां पुत्र वाशन्तीं परिसर्पसि। कुर्वंश्चाटुसहस्राणि अव्यक्तकलया गिरा॥१०४॥
व्यादितास्यः क्षुधार्तश्च पीतेनास्येन पुत्रक। शोणेन तालुना पुत्र कथमद्य न सर्पसि॥१०५॥
verses.english: "O, son why you are not nearing me today... why don't you make sweet sounds with your sweet voice... why you don't bite this fruit today with your yellow beak... why don't you eat this fruit with your reddish mouth... why not wiggle your wings to my delight... why I am not listening your pleasant chirping saying चि-ची-कू-ची... if not now, when can my motherly affection be fulfilled with a son like you... opening your mouth and wiggling your wings you used to ask for water... where is it now... all my motherly hopes are shattered with your passing..." thus that mother bird wailed a lot and then started questioning the king...

verses.sanskrit: पक्षाभ्यां त्वां परिष्वज्य ननु वाशामि चाप्यहम्। चीचीकूचीति वाशन्तं त्वामद्य न शृणोमि किम्॥१०६॥
मनोरथो यस्तु मम पश्येयं पुत्रकं कदा। व्यात्तास्यं वारि याचन्तं स्फुरत्पक्षं ममाग्रतः॥१०७॥
स मे मनोरथो भग्नस्त्वयि पञ्चत्वमागते। विलप्यैवं बहुविधं राजानमथ साब्रवीत्॥१०८॥
ननु मूर्धाभिषिक्तस्त्वं धर्मं वेत्सि सनातनम्। अद्य कस्मान्मम सुतं धात्र्या घातितवानसि॥१०९॥
तव पुत्रेण चाकृष्य क्षत्रियाधम शंस मे। न च नूनं श्रुता तेऽभूदियमाङ्गीरसी श्रुतिः॥११०॥
शरणागतः क्षुधार्तश्च शत्रुभिश्चाभ्युपद्रुतः। चिरोषितश्च स्वगृहे पातव्यः सर्वदा भवेत्॥१११॥
अपालयन्नरो याति कुम्भीपाकमसंशयम्। कथमस्य हविर्देवा गृह्णन्ति पितरः स्वधाम्॥११२॥
एवमुक्त्वा महाराज दशधर्मगता सती। शोकार्ता तस्य बालस्य चक्षुषी निर्बिभेद सा॥११३॥
verses.english: Saying so she that mother bird went into a state called tenfold-frenzy induced by her ecstatic wailing, Then, on puncturing the eyes of the son of brahmadatta with her talons and rendering him blind she dashed to sky...

verses.sanskrit: कराभ्यां राजपुत्रस्य ततस्तच्चक्षुरस्फुटत्। कृत्वा चान्धं नृपसुतमुत्पपात ततोऽम्बरम्॥११४॥
verses.bhavadeepa: “मत्तः प्रमत्त उन्मत्तः श्रान्तः क्रुद्धो बुभुक्षितः। त्वरमाणश्च भीतश्च लुब्धः कामी च ते दश॥” इति एतेषां दशानां धर्मो निर्विवेकित्वं गता प्राप्ता दशधर्मगता॥११३॥

verses.sanskrit: अथ राजा सुतं दॄष्ट्वा पूजनीयामुवाच ह। विशोका भव कल्याणि कृतं ते भीरु शोभनम्॥११५॥
गतशोका निवर्तस्व अजर्यं सख्यमस्तु ते। पुरेव वस भद्रं ते निवर्तस्व रमस्व च॥११६॥
verses.english: Even on seeing his son blinded that way, king brahmadatta spoke to the mother bird in this way, "you have justly requited like for like with my son... oh, lady-bird, be fearless and leave off your agony... you have done whatever you ought to... even though I am heartbroken for my son, I don't bear a grudge against you for whatever you have done to him... come back and stay with me as before...

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रपीडोद्भवश्चापि न कोपः परमस्त्वयि। ममास्ति सखि भद्रं ते कर्तव्यं च कृतं त्वया॥११७॥

पूजनीयोवाच।
              आत्मौपम्येन जानामि पुत्रस्नेहं तवाप्यहम्। न चाहं वस्तुमिच्छामि तव पुत्रमचक्षुषम्। कृत्वा वै राजशार्दूल त्वद्गृहे कृतकिल्बिषा॥११८॥
verses.english: "Committing the blunder of blinding your son, oh, kingly tiger, it will be unbefitting for me to stay further in your house... I am aware of your love for your soul-like son...

verses.sanskrit: गाथाश्चाप्युशनो गीता इमाः शृणु मयेरिताः। कुमित्रं च कुदेशं च कुराजानं कुसौहृदम्। कुपुत्रं च कुभार्यां च दूरतः परिवर्जयेत्॥११९॥
verses.english: You may list4en to शुक्र-नीति as I tell... a vile-friend, vile-country, vile-king, vile-friend, vile-son, vile-wife are discardable distantly...

verses.sanskrit: कुमित्रे सौहृदं नास्ति कुभार्यायां कुतो रतिः। कुतः पिण्डः कुपुत्रे वै नास्ति सत्यं कुराजनि॥१२०॥
verses.english: Where is amity with a vile-friend, where is the pleasure with a vile-wife, where is beatification with a vilely son, where is candour with a vile-king, where is trustfulness with a vilely person, where is livelihood in a vilest country! Threat haunts everywhere from a vile-king, while fret hangs around everything from a vile-son...

verses.sanskrit: कुसौहृदे क्व विश्वासः कुदेशे न तु जीव्यते। कुराजनि भयं नित्यं कुपुत्रे सर्वतोऽसुखम्॥१२१॥
अपकारिणि विस्रम्भं यः करोति नराधमः। अनाथो दुर्बलो यद्वन्न चिरं स तु जीवति॥१२२॥
न विश्वसेदविश्वस्ते विश्वस्ते नातिविश्वसेत्। विश्वासाद्भयमुत्पन्नं मूलान्यपि निकृन्तति॥१२३॥
राजसेविषु विश्वासं गर्भसङ्करितेषु च। यः करोति नरो मूढो न चिरं स तु जीवति॥१२४॥
verses.english: A fool reposing confidence in the officials of the king, or in the misbegotten nitwits, will not have a long-lived life...

verses.sanskrit: अप्युन्नतिं प्राप्य नृपात्प्रावारः कीटको यथा। स विनश्यत्यसन्देहमाहैवमुशना नृप॥१२५॥
अपि मार्दवभावेन गात्रं संलीय बुद्धिमान्। अरिं नाशयते नित्यं यथा वल्लिर्महाद्रुमम्॥१२६॥
verses.bhavadeepa: अपीति। प्रावारः पिपीलः ‘मुङ्गळा’ इति महाराष्ट्राः। स हि पूर्वमपक्ष एव पक्षोत्पत्तौ उत्पत्याधः पतन् पक्षिभिर्मार्यत इति प्रसिद्धम्। अन्ये तु प्रावारः पाश्चात्त्येषु पामर इति प्रसिद्धः। स किल कुड्यवृक्षागह्वरे प्राप्य उत्पद्यते स च पक्षोत्थाने सहसा उच्चैरुत्पत्य भूमौ पतितः पक्षिभिः खाद्यते तद्वदिति  व्याचख्युः॥१२५॥

verses.sanskrit: मृदुरार्द्रः कृशो भूत्वा शनैः संलीयते रिपुः। वल्मीक इव वृक्षस्य पश्चान्मूलानि कृन्तति॥१२७॥
अद्रोहसमयं कृत्वा मुनीनामग्रतो हरिः। जघान नमुचिं पश्चादपां फेनेन पार्थिव॥१२८॥
सुप्तं मत्तं प्रमत्तं वा घातयन्ति रिपुं नराः। विषेण वह्निना वाऽपि शस्त्रेणाप्यथ मायया॥१२९॥
न च शेषं प्रकुर्वन्ति पुनर्वैरभयान्नराः। घातयन्ति समूलं हि श्रुत्वेमामुपमां नृप॥१३०॥
शत्रुशेषमृणाच्छेषं शेषमग्नेश्च भूमिप। पुनर्वर्धेत सम्भूय तस्माच्छेषं न शेषयेत्॥१३१॥
हसते जल्पते वैरी एकपात्रे भुनक्ति च। एकासनं चारोहति स्मरते तच्च किल्बिषम्॥१३२॥
कृत्वा सम्बन्धकं चापि विश्वसेच्छत्रुणा न हि। पुलोमानं जघानाजौ जामाता सञ्शतक्रतुः॥१३३॥
निधाय मनसा वैरं प्रियं वक्तीह यो नरः। उपसर्पेन्न तं प्राज्ञः कुरङ्ग इव लुब्धकम्॥१३४॥
verses.english: indra is the son-in-law of पुलोम... be that as it may... the same indra eliminated पुलोम in a given war... enmity is intransigent... believing someone who comes nigh exchanging pleasantries by hiding hatred in heart is as good as adopting the syndrome 'hart-finding-a-credible-hunter...'

verses.sanskrit: न चासन्ने निवस्तव्यं सवैरे वर्धिते रिपौ। पातयेत्तं समूलं हि नदीरय इव द्रुमम्॥१३५॥
अमित्रादुन्नतिं प्राप्य नोन्नतोऽस्मीति विश्वसेत्। तस्मात्प्राप्योन्नतिं नश्येत्प्रावार इव कीटकः॥१३६॥
verses.english: One cannot remain in self-approbation with a monologic saying 'I am at the zenith...' that too, when that stature is fed upon the interests of his enemy... he and his stature are likely to fall like a winged ant who takes flight overconfident of its trifling wings

verses.sanskrit: इत्येता ह्युशनोगीता गाथा धार्या विपश्चिता। कुर्वता चात्मरक्षां वै नरेण पृथिवीपते॥१३७॥
मया सकिल्बिषं तुभ्यं प्रयुक्तमतिदारुणम्। पुत्रमन्धं प्रकुर्वन्त्या तस्मान्नो विश्वसे त्वयि॥१३८॥
एवमुक्त्वा प्रदुद्राव तदाऽऽकाशं पतङ्गिनी। इत्येतत्ते मयाख्यातं पुराभूतमिदं नृप॥१३९॥
ब्रह्मदत्तस्य राजेन्द्र यद्वृत्तं पूजनीयया। श्राद्धं च पृच्छसे यन्मां युधिष्ठिर महामते॥१४०॥
अतस्ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम्। गीतं सनत्कुमारेण मार्कण्डेयाय पृच्छते॥१४१॥
श्राद्धस्य फलमुद्दिश्य नियतं सुकृतस्य च। तन्निबोध महाराज सप्तजातिषु भारत॥१४२॥
सगालवस्य चरितं कण्डरीकस्य चैव हि। ब्रह्मदत्ततृतीयानां योगिनां ब्रह्मचारिणाम्॥१४३॥
verses.english: Oh, king धर्मज, now I will narrate further about the results occurring from the beatification of fatherly-gods, as has been said in the legends of seven-births of the sons of sage कौशिक॥ along with legends of yogi-s and ascetics like गालव, कण्डरीक and the थिर्द् ब्रह्मदत्त॥।
